question.problem:
A wireless headphone set includes $2$ earbuds (left and right) and a charging case.
The weights of the earbuds are normally distributed with mean $4\,\text{g}$ and a variance of $0.01\,{\text{g}}^{2},$ while the weights of charging cases are normally distributed with mean $38\,\text{g}$ and a variance of $0.14\,{\text{g}}^{2}.$

 If one headphone set is randomly selected, what is the probability that it weighs less than $45.8\,\text{g}?$ You may assume that the weights are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.8\,$ | $\,0.2119\,$ | $\,0.2090\,$ | $\,0.2061\,$ | $\,0.2033\,$ | $\,0.2005\,$ |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2420\,$ | $\,0.2389\,$ | $\,0.2358\,$ | $\,0.2327\,$ | $\,0.2296\,$ |
| $\,-0.6\,$ | $\,0.2743\,$ | $\,0.2709\,$ | $\,0.2676\,$ | $\,0.2643\,$ | $\,0.2611\,$ |
| $\,-0.5\,$ | $\,0.3085\,$ | $\,0.3050\,$ | $\,0.3015\,$ | $\,0.2981\,$ | $\,0.2946\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{1}$, ${X}_{2},$ and ${X}_{3}$ denote the weight of the charging case, and the weights of the left and right earbuds, respectively. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{1}∼N(38,0.14),\,{X}_{2}∼N(4,0.01),\,{X}_{3}∼N(4,0.01).
$$

Let the random variable $Y$ denote the weight of the headphone set. Then, we have

$$
Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+{X}_{3}.
$$

The random variable $Y$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =38+2\cdot 4 \\  & =46, \\ \text{Var}[Y] & =0.14+0.01+0.01 \\  & =0.16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
Y∼N(46,0.16).
$$

In order to find $P(Y<45.8),$ we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<45.8) & =P(Z<\frac{45.8-46}{\sqrt{0.16}}) \\  & =P(Z<-0.5)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(-0.5)≈0.3085.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<45.8) & =Φ(-0.5) \\  & =0.3085.\end{aligned}
$$
